question: ______ is the weakest of the acids listed below.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Acetic **____**acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Because it** partially dissociates into its constituent ions when acetic acid is dissolved in water, Acetic acid is a weak acid.**
 
• It is well known that this weak acid can mix miscible with water. In an aqueous solution, an acid called acetic acid ionises just marginally.
 
• A particularly popular weak acid is acetic acid, which is present in vinegar.
 
• **Acetic acid, commonly known as ethanolic acid,** is a liquid organic chemical that is colourless.
 
• The amount of the original acid that has been ionised in the solution is represented by the acid ionisation.
 
• As a result, the numerical value of Ka represents the acid's strength. Stronger acids than weaker acids with relatively lower Ka values include weak acids with substantially higher Ka values. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Fluorine-containing chemical compounds include **hydrogen fluoride.**
 
• It can exist as a colourless vapour, seething liquid, or as a substance that has been dissolved in water.
 
• Hydrofluoric acid is what hydrogen fluoride is known as when it dissolves in water.
 
• The inorganic substance **nitric acid** has the formula HNO₃.
 
• This mineral acid is extremely corrosive.
 
• One of the many industrial uses for **hydrochloric acid (HCl),** a colourless, potent mineral acid, is the creation of the hydrochloride salt when it is combined with an organic base.
